children: By Niket Nishant and Johann M Cherian

Brazilian stocks surged on Thursday and were on track for their strongest day in over seven weeks after data showed inflation eased in mid-November, helping investors shrug off the latest tariff threats from Washington.
The Bovespa index
was last up 4.4%, the biggest gainer in Latin America, while the real
strengthened 1.4% versus the US dollar and 2.1% versus the Mexican peso

The IPCA-15 consumer price index rose less than expected in the month through mid-November, data showed, raising investor expectations the local central bank could start considering lowering interest rates if the trend continues.

The gains could help investors look past the fresh tariff threat from the US. Washington proposed adding new tariffs on goods from Brazil on Wednesday, ​including a 10% duty on finished aircraft, arguing Brasilia had failed to rectify what it calls "unreasonable" trade practices.

Separately, Brazil's finance minister Dario Durigan said he will hold a follow-up meeting with President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva later on Thursday to discuss additional fiscal measures aimed at curbing spending.
MSCI's index of regional equities (.MILA00000PUS) gained 2.9%, while the corresponding currency gauge (.MILA00000CUS) rose 1.3%.

"EM equities look positioned for robust performance in 2027, supported by double-digit earnings growth, inexpensive valuations, an oversold starting point, and structural AI capex tailwinds," JPMorgan analysts wrote in a note.
The brokerage has an "overweight" rating on regional sovereign bonds, but is underweight currencies as it expects the US Federal Reserve to raise rates.
Higher rates in the US typically boost the dollar, thereby weakening emerging market currencies.
ARGENTINA'S SENATE POISED TO SUSPEND PRIMARIES
Argentine stocks (.MMXMRVLGA) shot up 3.2% and the peso
gained 0.2% as the country's Senate weighed a bill that would suspend primary elections.
If suspended it would be a potential win for President Javier Milei ahead of next year's presidential race as the country teeters on the brink of a recession.
Mexican stocks
shed 1.6% after logging the strongest daily jump since June in the previous session, while the peso
slipped 0.6%.

The country's central bank raised its 2026 economic growth forecast to 1.9% after stronger-than-expected activity in the third quarter, even as it warned investment is likely to remain subdued because of uncertainty over trade ties with the United States.

Separately, the country sought a meeting with US aviation authorities to discuss permits for SpaceX to use Mexican airspace and potentially relocate its launch activities, following tensions between Mexico City and Elon Musk's trillion-dollar company.
Peru's sol
and stocks (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) were steady after President Keiko Fujimori said the country will receive a $10 billion loan from the Inter-American Development Bank over four years.
Venezuelan bonds were also steady, following a two-day rally on debt restructuring hopes.

The country is also working on separate bridge loans with the US Treasury and Qatar to clear arrears owed to two regional development banks, a move that could unlock fresh multilateral financing for the cash-strapped country, sources told Reuters.

Elsewhere, Turkey's Finance Minister Mehmet Simsek said the country expects to complete work to meet MSCI's requirements by the end of December, ahead of the index provider's June 2027 deadline, as Ankara seeks to bring its capital markets in line with international standards after an investment funds crisis.
The country's equities index
closed up 0.8% earlier in the day.
Trading was relatively subdued because of the US Thanksgiving holiday.
